listingTitle: Separate async work from Spring initialization
title: Separate async work from Spring initialization
why: PostConstruct initialization runs before ordinary Spring asynchronous proxy interception, so Async on the same lifecycle method does not provide the requested proxy-based asynchronous execution.
suggestion: Keep initialization synchronous or call an asynchronous method on a separate managed bean after its proxy is available.
limitations: High-confidence findings bind canonical Spring Async and javax.annotation.PostConstruct or jakarta.annotation.PostConstruct through explicit imports, wildcard imports, or fully qualified names. The same-method lifecycle check requires a top-level nonabstract managed class proven by canonical stereotypes or an unambiguous Bean return type within a scoped Spring module.
Explicit per-module EnableAsync AspectJ mode suppresses this proxy-only warning. Separate-bean initializer calls do not receive this same-method warning.
Custom lifecycle mechanisms, composed annotations, dynamic build configuration, unresolved Maven properties or remote parents, and non-Java source are not resolved.
